title: Follow the Flow: On Information Flow Across Textual Tokens in Text-to-Image Models
status: ACL 2026, Volume 1: Long Papers, pp. 34139–34157; official proceedings verified
reading_scope: Read all main methods, experiments, discussion and limitations plus substantive Appendices A–H from page-marked PDF extraction; references inspected only for contextual identification. Table 4 rendered and visually checked.
intervention: Inference-time final text-encoder token representation patching: preserve or isolate selected contextualized tokens with pad-token replacement for analysis; mitigate known misinterpreted lexical items by replacing all corresponding token representations with the encoding of the item plus local modifiers in isolation. No parameter update.
benchmark: Main information-flow analysis: 1,053 filtered DrawBench/PartiPrompts prompts and 5 seeds per prompt; mitigation: 110 curated polysemy prompts with human-judged unambiguous intended meanings.
target_score: Percentage of prompts exhibiting wrong lexical interpretation, VLM evaluation of manually specified intended versus wrong meanings (AppA.5).
protection_score: No separately reported original-correct relation/all-other-fact retention endpoint for Table4. AppA.4 perceptual-binding filtering is an analysis filter, not post-patching relation preservation.

main_table.unit: percent prompts exhibiting leakage, lower better

findings: Encoder-side contextual token patching can correct substantial lexical semantic leakage without editing denoiser weights.
Cross-item flow can be legitimate contextual meaning or an unintended lexical interpretation; appearance alone is not a harm label.
Architecture matters: CLIP/EOS pooling weakens isolated-token interpretability; SANA information flow is analyzed, but Table4 mitigation is limited to FLUX variants.
overlap: Directly covers causal token intervention, conditional information-flow analysis, and practical semantic-leakage correction. It is a necessary simple baseline before proposing a diagnostic action-selection mechanism; does not itself establish the proposed per-case protected-relation and equal-budget decision endpoints.
limitations: Known target items and manually specified intended/wrong senses; no demonstrated automatic error-location/decision pipeline with matched budget.
Polysemy-driven lexical misinterpretation is narrower than arbitrary cross-entity visual identity leakage.
VLM scores are approximate; syntactically simple object-centric prompts restrict generalization.
No dedicated per-image already-correct relation preservation endpoint or full end-to-end cost comparator.

A generation change under padded/off-context representations identifies an intervention effect, not unique natural generator causal responsibility; closed-model behavior cannot identify encoder-level mechanisms.
Classifier redundancy prediction accuracy is not identical to demonstrated downstream image alignment gain from classifier-predicted pruning.
review: Public peer-review reports not inspected for this addendum.
